subject: physics
question_text: A quantum processor has demonstrated quantum supremacy. What does this term mean?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 8 (printed p.143). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: quantum supremacy (also called quantum advantage) is correctly defined as the point where a programmable quantum processor solves a problem no classical computer can solve in any practical amount of time; the book's named commercial processor is replaced with neutral wording per Rule 35.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: It is reached by a programmable
steps.why: The term names the moment a quantum processor first outperforms every classical computer on a chosen task, not a permanent state of computers in general.
common_mistakes: Writing that quantum computers are now better than all computers in general.
Leaving out the alternate name quantum advantage.
steps.memory_tip: Quantum supremacy equals quantum advantage: one processor, one task.
steps.margin_note: Both names, quantum supremacy and quantum advantage, are accepted.

steps.label: The condition

lines.text: No classical computer can solve it

lines: in any practical amount of time.
steps.why: This condition is what makes the achievement quantum supremacy rather than just a quantum computer being faster in general: no classical machine can finish the task at all in a reasonable time.
common_mistakes: Saying the classical computer takes longer instead of saying it takes an impractical amount of time.
Leaving out the word classical and only mentioning computers in general.
steps.memory_tip: The line to write: no classical computer finishes it in practical time.
steps.margin_note: State the comparison as classical computer versus quantum processor.
